note: Issue 438, institutional-contacts.md section 3 'His machines break'. Placeholder prose: the Author writes the real lines. The gunsmith's machines have broken, and he asks the sum the break named to mend them. Agreeing is a promise of gold to the TOWN (town-economy.md section 4): kept, the town's purse holds it and the machines are mended. Refused, ignored, or promised and then broken because the Crown refuses payments, and the gunsmith is dark for six months: the town makes no guns, the armoury's included. Unskippable: the consequence of silence is the whole of the letter, so the PC must see it.

body.text: The machines in the gunsmith's shop at {param:town} have broken, and the men cannot mend them from what we have.
{param:amount} would see them repaired. Without it the shop stands idle, and so does the armoury, for it works from the gunsmith's bored barrels and has nothing to finish without them.
It is to go to the town, which pays the smiths. I shall know within the month whether it has come.
I set down plainly what it costs to say no: half a year with no muskets made in {param:town}, whatever else happens in it.

tone.text: {sender:name} — as to the machines at {param:town}, I write {choice}.

options.label: the Crown will pay to mend them
options.text: The Crown will send it, to the town, for the machines.

options.label: the shop must wait
options.text: The Crown cannot find it now. The shop must stand until it can.
